how_to_use: To add a food, copy one whole item block, paste it before the closing bracket of items, and change the values; keep every field, in this order. name: the name you would search for, without the brand. brand: the restaurant or maker, or null for a generic dish. group: the heading the food is listed under, usually the brand or a dish type such as Home dish. category: one of supermarket (packaged goods), dining_out (restaurants and fast food) or whole_food (home dishes and basics). region_tags: where the item is sold as described, any of PH, US, UK, JP, KR. barcode: the digits printed under the barcode on the pack, or null when you do not have them. thumbnail_url: a web link to a small picture, or null. aka: other names and spellings to search by, plus the exact name of any older library entry this one replaces so the old one is hidden. serving: the usual portion as a label and its weight in grams, with grams set to null when the source gives no weight. extra_portions: other portion sizes of the same food with their gram weights, or an empty list. nutrition_per: says whether the numbers that follow are for the serving above (serving) or for 100 g of the food (100g). calories_kcal: energy in kilocalories. protein_g: protein in grams. carbs_g: total carbohydrate in grams. sugars_g: sugars in grams, or null when the source does not give them. fat_g: total fat in grams. saturates_g: saturated fat in grams, or null when the source does not give it. fibre_g: fibre in grams, or null when the source does not give it. sodium_mg: sodium, always in milligrams (if a label only shows salt in grams, multiply it by 400), or null. basis: official (published by the brand), database (from a nutrition database or food composition table) or estimate (worked out from typical recipes and portions). src: the web page the numbers came from, or null for an estimate with no source. notes: anything worth remembering, such as which country's figures these are. default_portion (optional; when used it goes right after extra_portions): which portion the app lists first with its calories. Leave it out and the app lists 100 g first, except for restaurant items, drinks, foods counted in units (egg, fruit, slice of bread, burger) and foods used by the spoon, which keep the serving above first. serving keeps the serving above first, 100g forces 100 g first (write the word in quotes).

items.name: Steamed white rice
items.notes: USDA SR Legacy: rice, white, long-grain, regular, enriched, cooked, no salt or fat added. One cup (158 g) is 205 kcal. Restaurant cups run roughly 140-200 g, so the 150 g portion is an assumption.

items.name: Garlic fried rice
items.notes: FatSecret Singapore generic sinangag, scaled from 163 kcal per 100 g to a cup of about 200 g. Oil varies a lot between cooks.

items.name: Chicken adobo
items.notes: FatSecret Singapore generic chicken adobo, about 141 kcal per 100 g. The source lists 1 cup at 345 kcal, which works out to about 244 g. Rice not included.

items.name: Pork sinigang
items.notes: FatSecret Singapore generic sinigang na baboy. This is a meat-heavy figure; a brothy bowl with less pork is lower.

items.name: Chicken tinola
items.notes: FatSecret Singapore generic tinolang manok, one bowl of about 249 g with chicken, green papaya or sayote and broth.

items.name: Boiled egg
items.notes: USDA SR Legacy: egg, whole, cooked, hard-boiled. One large egg (50 g, without shell) is 78 kcal.

items.name: Banana
items.notes: USDA survey food (FNDDS): banana, raw, peeled weight. The 126 g banana is the USDA standard size; lakatan and latundan are usually smaller, so weigh one if you want it exact. Saba (cooking banana) is a different entry.

items.name: Grilled chicken breast (skinless)
items.notes: USDA survey food (FNDDS): chicken breast, grilled without sauce, skin not eaten. Cooked weight without bone; the sodium figure assumes it was salted during cooking.

items.name: Pandesal
items.notes: FatSecret Singapore generic pandesal, one 45 g roll. A small bakery pandesal of about 30 g is roughly 90 kcal.

items.name: Chickenjoy 1 pc (thigh)
items.notes: US figures from the Jollibee USA nutrition sheet (the older library has no Philippine figures for it), so local pieces may differ in size. Chicken only, without rice or gravy. A drumstick (85 g) is 220 kcal and has its own library entry.

items.name: Jolly Spaghetti
items.notes: One regular serving as listed on FatSecret Singapore, which gives no weight. The much larger US serving (411 g) is 610 kcal.

items.name: Big Mac
items.notes: McDonald's Singapore figures, the nearest market with published numbers (the older library has no Philippine figures for it). The burger differs by country, so this entry is tagged for the Philippines only.

items.name: Chicken Inasal Paa (large)
items.notes: Estimate from typical portions: Mang Inasal publishes nothing. Worked out from about 140 g of edible roasted chicken leg meat and skin (the USDA figures linked) plus 1 tsp chicken oil. Rice and extra chicken oil are not included; other trackers say 350-415 kcal.

items.name: Flat White (tall)

serving.label: 1 tall (12 fl oz), hot, whole milk

items.notes: Starbucks Philippines figures, from its beverage nutrition table dated 3 November 2026 (tall, hot, whole milk, 262 g). Starbucks Philippines does not list protein; the 8.5 g here is calculated from the calories left after fat and carbohydrate. In the same table a grande (390 g) is 216 kcal and a venti (485 g) is 274 kcal.

items.name: Xiao Long Bao (pork)
items.notes: Estimate from typical recipes and portions: Din Tai Fung does not publish nutrition figures. Assumes about 21 g per piece (5 g flour wrapper, 16 g pork and broth filling), which gives roughly 200 kcal for 5 pieces and 400 kcal for 10. Dipping sauce is not included.

items.name: Ramen bowl with meat and egg
items.notes: USDA survey food (FNDDS): an average restaurant-style ramen with noodles, broth, meat and egg, US figures. The 2-cup bowl size is an assumption (bowls run about 2 to 2.5 cups), and a rich tonkotsu broth will be higher than this average.

items.name: Salmon nigiri sushi
items.notes: USDA survey food (FNDDS): sushi, topped with salmon (seasoned rice with a slice of raw salmon), US figures. Soy sauce is not included.

items.name: Samgyupsal (grilled pork belly)
items.notes: Plain grilled pork belly: the same FatSecret Singapore figures as the library's Inihaw na liempo entry, since Korean barbecue pork belly is the same cut grilled without marinade. Count cooked meat only; dipping sauces, sesame oil, rice and side dishes are not included.

items.name: Pad Thai with chicken
items.notes: USDA survey food (FNDDS): Pad Thai with chicken, US figures. The 2-cup plate size is an assumption; restaurant plates vary and oilier versions run higher.

items.name: Manager's Choice thin crust pizza (1 slice)
aka: Shakey's Manager's Choice thin crust (1 slice)

serving.label: 1 slice of a Large thin crust pizza (1/8 of the pie)

items.notes: Shakey's Philippines figures: a whole Large thin crust is 1,708 kcal, so one of 8 slices is 213 kcal. A Regular slice is 158 kcal and a Party slice 233 kcal.

items.name: Lucky Me! Pancit Canton Kalamansi
items.notes: Kalamansi flavour as listed on FatSecret Singapore: one 60 g pack (dry weight) prepared with its seasoning and oil. Barcode not recorded yet; add the digits from your pack. This source does not give sugars, saturated fat or sodium.

items.name: SkyFlakes Crackers
items.notes: Label values as recorded on Open Food Facts. The barcode is the one on that Open Food Facts page and may be an export pack, so check it against your own pack.

items.name: Argentina Corned Beef
items.notes: Label serving as recorded on Open Food Facts; oil used for sauteing is not included. The barcode is the one on that Open Food Facts page, so check it against your own can.

items.name: Tender Juicy Hotdog (regular)
items.notes: Purefoods Tender Juicy label values as recorded on Open Food Facts, one 34 g regular piece; frying oil is not included. The jumbo weight is approximate (roughly 175 kcal). The barcode is the one on that Open Food Facts page, so check it against your own pack.

items.name: Coca-Cola Original
items.notes: Coca-Cola Philippines label: 100 kcal per 237 ml, scaled to a 355 ml can. The recipe differs in other countries, so this entry is tagged for the Philippines only.
